Really a tale of two sets of players from the Bucks perspective. Giannis Antetokounmpo, Myles Turner, AJ Green, Kyle Kuzma and Ryan Rollins played rather well, especially in the second half. Jericho Sims, Cole Anthony, Bobby Portis, Gary Trent Jr., and Gary Harris got clobbered.

Kyle Kuzma: Gotta start with Kyle Kuzma. This was a great game from him. He did everything the Bucks need him to in that position. He defended (4 steals btw), he rebounded (10 rebounds and he was not usually the problem boxing out), he cut, he kept the ball moving, he took his wide open 3s with confidence and knocked 2/4 down, and he busted his ass in transition. This is the Kyle Kuzma the Bucks need. Doc did a smart thing planting Myles on the perimeter and letting Kuzma take those cuts. He's just a bit of a more dynamic roller than Myles and this year it seems like he figured out that midrange shots are not for him. I think that is the biggest step here. The way he was using cuts to collapse the defense was really effective even if he wasn't the recipient of the pass. He showed off some soft hands on the catches too. An impressive game from Kuzma.

Giannis: get this guy a call lmao. He took a flying elbow to the chest on a rebound and just shrugged it off like a monster. Complete game from him. Don't even care about the attempted game winner being an ugly play where he just hucked that shit. Absolutely diced up the Hornets defense. His passes were on-time on-target and defense breaking. He made some big defensive plays but overall has just been good on that end. 18 assists is just crazy. Hornets had no answer for him.

Myles Turner: I think he's in a better fitting role offensively this game than he has been in the past. I said it when he was on Indiana, and it's still true today, if there is a defender squared up to Myles, in a stance, and between him and the basket, he cannot do anything. His drive game is not very good, he can get show and go blowbys but that's about it. Watching him see a center between him and the basket on a drive means he's going to take a difficult shot. He just doesn't have the shake to get by guys. So it makes sense to put him where his strengths are: let him shoot 3s and set screens around the perimeter on dribble hand-offs. Don't put him in dynamic positions with the ball, he's a play finisher. Came up big in overtime. Love The Antlers celebration.

Ryan Rollins: How can you not love Stickyfingers' game? It's wild how much he's improved from last year. Last year I often categorized him as 'not the problem', he wasn't hurting them but he wasn't doing all that much to lift them up either. Very reliant on others and sort of just another guy. This year he's driving to the bucket and finishing well, he's taking and making the midrange shots the defense gives him. He plays the pick and roll well with several rollers. He hasn't quite got entry passes and lobs down still but he can throw just about every other standard point guard pass. He feels automatic when Giannis hits him in the shooting pocket.

AJ Green: if this mfer could defend without fouling (not even be a good defender just one that doesn't foul) he'd be one cold white boy. High energy. He has a sort of gravity of his own. He sets screens and he figured out how to counter the Hornets running at him when he comes to set the screen by flopping. Not the most elegant counter, but you do what works I suppose. If he's the worst defender on the team, the Bucks are in a good spot. The problem is that he is not the worst defender on the team. Also can we run plays for him? They get good looks every time. We know they can cater to their players. Get AJ some easy ones. The team runs those plays well.

And now for something completely different.

Cole Anthony: this guy either has it or he doesn't. When he doesn't have it, it's painful. And when he does have it, it's still painful but just on defense. He's so small. He cannot navigate a screen to save his life  and he is the premier matador defender on the Bucks, and that's beating out some stiff competition. I've resigned myself to accepting that he's just not very good so I'll try to enjoy the flashy plays when they hit. It'll be nice for the Bucks to get healthy to knock him a few pegs down in the rotation. He's just too small on defense. On offense, I think good defenders will shut him down. It'll be good for the Bucks when they can afford to play him fewer minutes.

Bobby Portis: speaking of affording to play him fewer minutes. Bobby does what he's always done: nothing on defense, decent shooting and good post-moves. It's not all that valuable to the team right now but we've seen Bobby be more effective than this for years. This is also the smallest role the Bucks have asked him to play and his production has gone down accordingly and then some. I think he'll pick it back up, but I'd like to see Doc try to figure out some ways to keep the ball on the perimeter instead of charging down the lane at 'rim defender' Bobby Portis. I think this game was a good example of the size of the role he should have. Now it's up to the coaches to keep him there and it's up to Bobby to excel in his new role.

Gary Trent Jr.: the ¡Olé! Apprentice himself. Gary loves gambling for steals. Gary has had real trouble keeping the ball in front of him. Gary has not been navigating screens well. Gary hasn't been a big part of the offense either. It feels like roster construction has sort of got his ass alongside his downswing in ability. AJ and Gary Trent Jr. cannot play together. I'd rather have AJ out there with Giannis. It seems as simple as that. Hope it's just like last year where Gary starts out the season poorly and then continues to get better and better as the season goes on. For now: woof.

Jericho just has rocks for hands, poor defensive instincts and the guards don't give him a fighting chance the way they let the ball charge downhill. Moves Bobby to the 4 so I expect to see more Jericho. I think there's a role here if Jericho can reach out and grab it.

He's a sharpshooter but the Bucks have like 4 guys encroaching on that role and only one of them can get the kick-out catch and shoot 3s that Giannis creates.

As a neutral, the most frustrating thing about watching the Celtics play was when they turned down obvious lay-ups for a kick-out 3.

I saw several instances of a Celt having beat their man to the rim or an opportunity for a wide open pass (Queta) that would've led to a guaranteed dunk or or lay-up. Instead, they kicked it out for a 3. In fairness, some of the 3's were relatively open, but the guaranteed 2 was the better shot.

The missed shots narrative is easy analysis, but I think if the Celtics just converted the basic lay-ups they created, they would've won by double digits.

It's like they were programmed to kick it out regardless of where they were or what other shot was available.

at the end of the day there are several takeaways from this season:

-
the celtics did not win a championship by shooting 3s endlessly, they won it by moving the ball so much that other teams couldn't defend it, and their shots became open

-
they also won with defence at the highest level, something which was missing on this team with the absence of a first rate centre.

-
the celtics were never supposed to be successful this season. losing in the first round after being up 3-1 is embarrassing. both these things are true.

-
pre-season predictions ranged from lottery, to lower play-in, to 5th-6th seed status and they managed to win 56 games. doing so after losing kristaps porzingis, al horford, jrue holiday, and luke kornet (as well as a number of other bench players) was an admirable effort.\

-
brad and joe have a talent for identifying players that have struggled and turning them into success stories. celtics now have walsh, gonzales, scheierman, queta, and garza playing regular minutes and doing well at it. they've experienced actual playoff pressure for the first time, and they'll know what to expect next time.

JJ Redick’s gameplan of maximum defensive pressure on SGA by denying him the ball every possession and then doubling to force him into bad passes and turnovers was excellent. Mark Daigneault had a similar strategy of targeting Austin Reaves to prevent him from being the second option.
